chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr, from Hisham and 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Miskan all together, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who hired a wet nurse and gave his child to her, and the child was with her. Then the wet nurse went away and hired another woman, and the wet nurse disappeared with the child, so it was not known what she did with him. He عليه السلام said: "The full blood money is due."

key_terms.ظِئْرًا: a wet nurse hired to suckle and care for an infant
key_terms.لَا يُدْرَى: it is not known or cannot be determined
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةُ: financial compensation for wrongful death or loss of life
key_terms.ٱلْوَلَدِ: the child entrusted to the wet nurse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a wet nurse disappears with a child and the child’s fate is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning liability when a hired wet nurse disappears with a child and the child's fate becomes unknown. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the full diyah is due, establishing full financial liability in such a case.
